pr_body:
Should this also handle the hardcoded wrap options as well?
```
  {"aes192-wrap", OPT_AES192_WRAP, '-', "Use AES192 to wrap key"},
    {"aes256-wrap", OPT_AES256_WRAP, '-', "Use AES256 to wrap key"},
# ifndef OPENSSL_NO_DES
    {"des3-wrap", OPT_3DES_WRAP, '-', "Use 3DES-EDE to wrap key"},
# endif
    {"wrap", OPT_WRAP, 's', "Any wrap cipher to wrap key"},

```

If so, what are the official names for the wrapping ciphers?  And should the `no_des` ifdef be removed? From here?  From all apps?
pr_comments:
> Unfortunately, this introduces a leak.

And cleaning it up becomes a REAL pain,  const/non-const, etc.  It would be *great* if the EVP types had a built-in flag so that you could always call free and it would be ignore if you were returning a built-in global.  Sigh.
I believe that the proper solution for this is Rich wrote.

> I believe that the proper solution for this is Rich wrote.

I've considered that before, but quite frankly, ewwwww.  Basically, what you're suggesting is to have application deliberately break constness somewhere...  I can see how that will fly

I am willing to do the add-flag thing if the OTC is in favor.

I don't like breaking const.  More importantly, tho, having to do things like you show above in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/14182#discussion_r575867943 is even worse.  But this is just a matter of style and taste, and the OMC needs to decide because it is holding up other work (like this PR).
You gotta remember that this "fix" is also transitional.  In some future, fetching will be the only recourse, so the question is how far you want to go to be able to "nicely" support legacy stuff...
If the fix is temporary, then the cleaner thing to do is add the flag.

> If so, what are the official names for the wrapping ciphers? And should the `no_des` ifdef be removed? From here? From all apps?

SP800-38F says it is Key Wrap

> Basically, what you're suggesting is to have application deliberately break constness somewhere... I can see how that will fly

So in this case opt_md for example should not return a const EVP_MD*.

const EVP_MD should have flag that is off.. The fetch sets the flag for the dynamic case.. 

Seems like a reasonable idea to me.

> So in this case opt_md for example should not return a const EVP_MD*.

So, does that mean that we change `EVP_get_digestbyname()` to return a non-const `EVP_MD *`?
Or does that mean that we un-const its return value in `opt_md()`?
Also, is that what you'd recommend other applications to do?

> > So in this case opt_md for example should not return a const EVP_MD*.
> 
> So, does that mean that we change `EVP_get_digestbyname()` to return a non-const `EVP_MD *`?
> Or does that mean that we un-const its return value in `opt_md()`?
> Also, is that what you'd recommend other applications to do?

Ahh ok, changing EVP_get_digestbyname() to non const sounds like a bad idea..
If opt_md() is making a choice between a const/ non const then it would need to cast.
We already had to change the code to add the fetch, so that is the point where you need to do the cast if you need both.
This would then propogate to anywhere where you had to do the selection and then free (which we have in quite a few places already).

Mostly agree with @slontis's comment at https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/14182#issuecomment-778870130 but I'd make the local variable non-const.

As for what advice to give developers, that's up to the project to decide.  If it doesn't like my "don't free me" flag in the structure, it'll have to decide what to do instead.

> SP800-38F says it is Key Wrap

Yeah, but I was thinking of 'openssl official' as in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/evp/e_aes.c#L3625

I don't understand the talk about const/non-const.  The flag will be fixed in the structures EVP_get_digestbyname() returns, they are not going to be modified.  Sure a cast will be required when freeing them but the underlying memory won't be altered.

Adding a flag and insisting on some casts is a small price compared to having additional arguments to functions or carrying two pointers everywhere.  We've already got cases where we've a _fetched_ pointer and the _real_ pointer, they are ugly.

> I don't understand the talk about const/non-const. 

I think you're looking for more than there is.  IT's all about sometimes you get a const pointer via `EVP_xxx()` or `EVP_get...byname()` or sometimes you get a pointer via a `fetch` call.  And as you point out, when you have to do a mix of things (as in the apps and other code), it's yucky.

So far @levitte has been arguing against cast-away-const, and others feel the pain of the current code isn't worth it.

We could hide the cast away of const inside the free call.  I don't like this as much as making folks cast it away in their code because we will be changing to the non-const version eventually.

People who grab the algorithm via `EVP_xxx()` aren't going to be freeing it.  Those who update their code to fetch will be.  The majority of the cases where both forms are necessary will be in our libraries.  Let's make it easy for us right now....
Do note the little detail that we don't need an extra flag, the `prov` pointer is already there to save the day...

> Do note the little detail that we don't need an extra flag, the `prov` pointer is already there to save the day...

Even better :)

So this snipped of code (https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/9dc9c7f2d7f25e100dd7d80e9bc51e205033cd8c/apps/speed.c#L1498-L1528) and corresponding `free` operations (https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/9dc9c7f2d7f25e100dd7d80e9bc51e205033cd8c/apps/speed.c#L4137-L4140) can be simplified?

BTW, I believe that EVP_XXX_fetch() should be a fallback after EVP_get_yyyyyybyname() fails, not the other way around.
The reason is that if an engine is loaded and implements an alternative for an algorithm that we have in our default provider, the engine code will never be used.  That will be a surprise.
Fair point, but almost everywhere in code I remember that we try to fetch first...

> Fair point, but almost everywhere in code I remember that we try to fetch first...

Not quite...  there are a few places where, if we don't have prior knowledge, we have a look at whatever's available from engines *first*.  I haven't looked much at what happens with speed, so I hadn't noticed that it does it the other way around.  It would be interesting to know what happens if we try speed with, say, the padlock engine...

Speaking of what we're currently talking about, I expect to see that fixed in a *separate commit*, as that has nothing to do with cipher-wrap per se.  It should be marked with 'Fixes #14178' and 'Fixes #14179'.  That may actually make it suitable to be a separate PR.
My plan would be to add the flag and change `opt_cipher` and `opt_md` to not return `const` values, and then always call the `EVP_xxx_free` function.

> My plan would be to add the flag

Did you catch on that it's not necessary?  Why add redundant information?

@levitte Could you please submit the patch from the comment above 
as a PR? As that change would be useful for my hacking of speed command as well.
Sure
It turns out that @richsalz has a point with a flag.  an EVP_MD is not only created with EVP_MD_fetch(), but also with EVP_MD_meth_new().
I'll take the rest of the discussion in #14178 and #14179, this PR has been derailed enough as it is.

I have a PR coming that cleans up and standardizes all the `EVP_xxx_free` routines.  It looks like they all work as-is, except for `EVP_MD_free` which needs the flag and is what I had been looking at. :)
@richsalz please see what I wrote in #14179.
This is on-hold until #14194 gets merged and then I'll either update it or abandon it.

> This is on-hold...

Er, ok, so the original intention with this PR, to have cipher-wrap fetched after providers are loaded, has somehow lost its value?
I am only inclined to rebase once, and since there's other work happening in the apps I'm waiting.
Ah, sorry, quoted the wrong thing.  It was the mention of abandoning that surprised me.

>  It was the mention of abandoning that surprised me.

Just trying to be completely realistic.

Refreshing this since the OTC decided on an approach and #14193 was approved and merged.  Most of the discussion here can be ignored now. There are still a couple of open questions:
- Should the hardcoded cipher-wrap options be handled this way also? https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/14182#issue-573141714
- What are the "official" names (to be used for lookup/fetch) of those cipher-wraps?
- Should we remove the impact of the `no_des` flag since leaving it out of openssl still means another provider can do it.
Removed "WIP" and made it a draft, since that seems to be the thing to do these days. Let me know if not.
Waiting on answers from the OMC https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/14182#issuecomment-821999931

> Refreshing this since the OTC decided on an approach and #14193 was approved and merged. Most of the discussion here can be ignored now. There are still a couple of open questions:
> 
>     * Should the hardcoded cipher-wrap options be handled this way also? [#14182 (comment)](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/14182#issue-573141714)
> 
>     * What are the "official" names (to be used for lookup/fetch) of those cipher-wraps?
> 
>     * Should we remove the impact of the `no_des` flag since leaving it out of openssl still means another provider can do it.

I do not think there is anything controversial here that would require OMC vote.

Answers IMO are:
1. yes
2. please look at the default provider - the first name of the algorithm is supposed to be the "canonical" name as we see it. Of course opinion of other provider authors might differ and that's the reason we allow multiple names. However they should at least include our "canonical" name as an alias if they want to be compatible
3. yes, if you want to, however I do not think this is a blocker for 3.0 at all
This now depends on #15011
Rebased against master and updated commit pushed.

issue_context.title: [master] 'openssl enc' can't access ciphers that libcrypto doesn't know about
issue_context.body:
I played a bit with external providers that offer ciphers that libcrypto doesn't know about, and that fails.
This is due to `opt_cipher()` (in `apps/lib/opt.c`) only tries to get the cipher with `EVP_get_cipherbyname()`, never with `EVP_CIPHER_fetch()`.
